title: Joys and hopes (Gaudium et Spes)
hookLine: the joys and hopes, griefs and anxieties of people today are the Church's too

lines: A JOY AND A GRIEF AT ONCE.
cards: Two messages land in the same group chat a minute apart. One friend got engaged: ring photo, three exclamation marks. Another got a scan result back and needs someone to talk to tonight.

A thumb hovers between a party emoji and a heart. That split second, holding a joy and a grief at once, is close to how the Second Vatican Council chose to open its conversation with the modern world.
Its first words became its name.

teach.h: GAUDIUM ET SPES: JOY AND HOPE.
teach.b: The document is the Pastoral Constitution on the Church in the Modern World, and in Latin it begins Gaudium et Spes: joy and hope. Here's its opening thought, paraphrased.
The joys and the hopes, the griefs and the anxieties of people today, especially the poor and anyone who suffers, are the joys and hopes, griefs and anxieties of Christ's followers too.
Nothing truly human, it says, fails to find an echo in their hearts. Notice three things about that sentence. First, the order.
It begins with joy. The council didn't open by listing the world's sins; it opened by claiming the world's happiness as its own. Second, the pairs.
Joys sit next to griefs, hopes next to anxieties. The Church is asked to carry both, the engagement and the scan.
Third, the people singled out: especially the poor, and anyone who suffers.
The rest of the document goes on to marriage and family, culture, work and the economy, politics, war and peace, always with that opening as the lens.
It also asks the Church to read what it calls the signs of the times. Saint Paul had already said it in one line, in the Douay-Rheims: "Rejoice with them that rejoice; weep with them that weep."
And to the Galatians: "Bear ye one another's burdens; and so you shall fulfil the law of Christ."

how: Catholics bring the needs of the world into the Prayer of the Faithful at Mass, pray for the sick and the grieving by name, and point to Gaudium et Spes when describing the Church's care for the poor and for public life.

games.why: Gaudium et Spes begins with joy and hope, and claims the joys and griefs of people today, especially the poor, as its own.

practice: Let one person come to mind who's carrying something heavy right now, a diagnosis, a debt, a child who won't call, a job hanging by a thread, and hold them and the worry without trying to fix it.
If you pray, name them before God and leave the rest unsaid; if you don't, simply keep them company in your mind. Then let someone's good news come to mind too, and be glad with them.
